correctness.rationale: C=PASS. Reconstructed the all-integer/all-parameter theorem for m>=3, 1<beta<m^2/(2m-1), lambda>0 from all six frozen source files. Complex differentiation gives rho_(z zbar)=m^2|z|^(2m-2)+beta(2m-1)Re(z^(2m-2))+(m+1)^2|z|^(2m), bounded below by [m^2-beta(2m-1)]|z|^(2m-2)+(m+1)^2|z|^(2m)>0 for z!=0; rho_(w wbar)=1. The |z|^(2m+2) and |w|^2 terms bound the domain. Weighted real flow satisfies exactly rho(e^-t z,e^-mt w)=e^(-2mt)(rho+1)-1+(e^(-(2m+2)t)-e^(-2mt))|z|^(2m+2), hence strict boundary derivative -2m-2|z|^(2m+2), smooth boundary, global positive-real inward flow, and connectivity via contraction. Only possibly weak boundary points are {z=0,|w|=1}; their H^2 measure vanishes, so the Sibony B-regularity criterion explicitly invoked in Dao–Nguyen–Tran Example 1.8 applies. Compactness, a uniform negative normal derivative and bounded imaginary coefficient of the complex directional derivative produce the narrow complex sector, uniform boundary depth c|tau|, self-map, and displacement O(|tau|) in SID Definition 1.4. The reduced divisor splits as (w-1-sqrt(lambda)z)(w-1+sqrt(lambda)z), intersects the domain at (t,1-sqrt(lambda)t), and its unique singular point p=(0,1) is on the boundary and escapes with f(S_tau p)=(e^(-m tau)-1)^2, order two. Nonconvexifiability follows from absence of supporting complex graphs eta=h(z): for leading order k<2m a harmonic sign change contradicts support; k>2m leaves negative P rays; at k=2m the 2m-2 negative directions theta_j=pi/(2m-2)+j*pi/(m-1) have sum exp(i2m theta_j)=0, so one ray retains negative leading boundary value. Thus any putative local holomorphic convexification would pull back an impossible support hyperplane. Dao–Nguyen–Tran Theorem 1.7 then gives extended-real continuity of the divisor Green function and canonical envelope limits. The paper normalizes ||f||_closure<=1 by a nonzero constant; for the unnormalized f_lambda, translation equivariance of P_Omega and the shifted logarithmic truncation index recover the same limiting assertions, with desingularized Green function shifted compatibly. Symbolic spot-checks for m=3,4,7 confirm the Levi/Euler/root-orbit algebra, while the proofs and the cited theorem apply to all m; no finite sample is presented as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge PASS for the simultaneous all-m bounded B-regular nonconvexifiable family with a global sectorial weighted flow and continuous hypersurface Green functions, not for either the abstract SID theorem or KN local non-support geometry alone. Dao–Nguyen–Tran (arXiv:2610.00909v1) Theorem 1.7 establishes the abstract implication and Example 1.8 explicitly treats the single m=4, beta=15/7 member with exactly the same divisor/flow; its end question asks for broader classes. Zhao–Han–Li 2013, quoted as Theorem 1 in Hu et al. 2025, already gives general unbounded KN polynomial pseudoconvexity and local nonsupport for p=2m, q=2m-2, 1<beta<=m^2/(2m-1). Those historical ingredients cannot be claimed original. The inspected sources do not state or automatically supply the bounded radial stabilization, its verified global complex-sector inward displacement/depth, divisor escape and Green continuity simultaneously for all m and open beta intervals. Resultary returned the audited finding itself as its closest hit; that same record has no independent priority force. value.rationale: V=PASS with bounded scope. The fresh primary Green-continuity paper explicitly asks for broader nonconvexifiable classes bearing a global holomorphic inward deformation. The candidate answers that motivated geometric gap for infinitely many distinct finite types 2m, each with a genuine open beta interval, proving global boundedness, B-regularity and complex-sector flow rather than merely local polynomial pseudoconvexity. It also verifies the reduced translated crossing divisor and singular escape needed to invoke the hypersurface Green theorem, yielding canonical truncation convergence. The payoff is a reusable weighted-homogeneous construction and a complete parameterized class; known m=4 example and general local support results are credited. The value judgment does not assert maximal beta range, arbitrary divisors, an independent continuity theorem, or novel local KN geometry; the flow and continuity extension are mathematically motivated by the original source question.
